resources.string: On the computer running Gecko, open the palette and pick Open on another device. Scan the QR code it shows, or paste its link here.\n\nThe phone needs to reach that computer: the same Wi-Fi, or Tailscale.
Scan QR code from a picture
Point at the QR code in Gecko\'s Open on another device
There\'s no QR code in that picture that could be read.
Link (paste a new one to change the token)
Its tabs keep running on the computer. You can add it again by scanning its QR code.
%1$s\n\nIs the phone on the same network or tailnet, and is Gecko listening on it (gecko daemon --listen 0.0.0.0:7681)? You can save it now and connect later.
That link has no access token in it. Use the link or QR code from Open on another device on the computer itself, or run gecko url there.
This machine\'s token couldn\'t be read on this phone. Scan its QR code again.
Gecko refused the token. It changes when Gecko is set up again: scan the QR code again.
%1$s isn\'t on a private network, so Gecko\'s token would cross the internet unencrypted. Use https there (for example tailscale serve 7681), or the machine\'s LAN or Tailscale address.
A coding agent in a Gecko tab is waiting for your answer, or finished.
Shown while Gecko stays connected to notify you.

resources.string: Gecko will notify you when an agent needs you.
Notifications are off for Gecko. Turn them on in Android\'s settings.
Gecko stays connected in the background and notifies you when an agent needs you.
Android stops apps it doesn\'t see on screen. To notify you while Gecko is closed, it keeps a small connection to your machines open and shows a notification that it does.
